description: Status, where it came from (origin: the import source, the export of which timeline_id and preset, or the create.* tool and the media it was made from), a signed download url for the file (media is kept 7 days after last use: save the file from it to keep it, and media.import it again later) and a page_url that plays or shows it in any browser (to give a person), its format (extension and mime_type, read from the file, not its name), everything the probe read (probe: the format and every stream, e.g. pix_fmt, colour space, primaries, transfer), duration, frame rate, conform reasons, integrated loudness and summaries of media.analyze results under analyses (counts only: analyses.transcript.words is how many words). include returns those results at the top level, e.g. include ["transcript"] gives transcript.words, the list of words with times. For long media, read them in pieces: from_seconds and to_seconds keep what overlaps that stretch of the media, offset and limit page through what is left, and pages says, per analysis, the index of the first item returned in the whole list (for transcript words, the index clip.add source {words} takes), how many matched and next_offset for the next page (null at the end).

from_seconds.description: Only what ends after this media time: transcript words, beats, face and look frames

include.description: Also return these analyses (otherwise only their summaries): in full, or the piece from_seconds, to_seconds, offset and limit choose

limit.description: At most this many items of each included list; pages says where the next starts

media_id.description: Media handle from media.import or a create.* tool

offset.description: Skip this many items of each included list (after the time range)

to_seconds.description: Only what starts before this media time

name: media.get

analyses.description: Summaries of media.analyze results (counts, not data); include puts each in full at the top level

look.description: frames and questions: the latest run

sounds.description: heard: the sounds the latest run found at or above its min_probability

words.description: How many words; the words themselves are in transcript.words

conform.description: Why a mezzanine was made (vfr, rotation, hdr, codec); empty when not needed

created_at.description: When it was imported or made

expires_at.description: When url and page_url stop working

extension.description: The extension its format takes (.png, .mp4), from the file itself, not its name

font_family.description: Fonts: the family; use font_media_id in a text style to set text in it

media_id.description: Media handle from media.import or a create.* tool

origin.description: Where it came from, to tell one version from another: the import source, the export of which timeline, or the create.* tool and the media it was made from

attached.description: url: the file the user attached in the chat, passed as media.import file

file_name.description: upload: the name the file was sent with

from.description: upload: a file the user sent; url: downloaded; path: a media root; render: an export.video; created: a create.* tool

job_id.description: render: the export.video job; created: the create.* job

media_ids.description: created: the media it was made from (a cutout's source, a page's assets)

items.description: Media handle from media.import or a create.* tool

path.description: path: the file it was imported from

range.description: render: the frames exported, when not the whole timeline

recipe.description: created: a hash of what it was made from; the same recipe makes the same media

sources.description: render: where each stretch of this file comes from, per track, read from the timeline when it was exported (kept after the timeline expires). With a speed curve, source_in and source_out are the clip's whole source range

speed.description: The clip's speed change, as clip.set_speed set it

track_id.description: Track of the timeline; outer/inner inside a nested one

timeline_id.description: render: the timeline that was exported

tool.description: created: the create.* tool that made it

url.description: url: the address it was downloaded from, without its query string

via.description: upload: sent through a media.upload link, dropped on the account page, or a data: URI

page_url.description: media.get: a page that plays or shows the file in any browser, with no sign-in, to give a person; works until expires_at

first.description: Index in the whole list of the first item returned (transcript: the word index clip.add source {words} takes)

list.description: The list paged: transcript.words, beats.beats, faces.frames, speech.probabilities (one per frame_seconds from `from`), or look runs[].frames (each run is cut the same way; first and the counts are the latest run's)

matching.description: Items in the time range (the whole list without one)

next_offset.description: The offset that gives the next page of this range, or null at its end

pages.description: media.get with a range, offset or limit: per included analysis, which piece of its list came back

probe.description: media.get: everything FFprobe read from the file, as it gives it: the format and every stream (codec, pix_fmt, color_space, color_primaries, color_transfer, color_range, bit depth, sample rate, channel layout, tags, side data). Not for fonts and LUTs

sounds.description: With include ["sounds"]: the latest media.analyze sounds run, every probability included

peaks.description: Per sound reported: the highest probability it reaches anywhere

scores.description: Every probability, for your own cut-off or arithmetic

start_seconds.description: Where the first value starts: media seconds, or timeline seconds for a timeline

step_seconds.description: Seconds each value covers: 0.04 (every frame) unless asked or too long

values.description: Per sound, the highest probability in each step, 0 to 1

end.description: Where it ends, on the same clock

peak_seconds.description: The middle of the most likely frame

start.description: Where the run of matching 40 ms frames starts: media seconds, or timeline seconds for a timeline

spans.description: Per sound: the runs of 40 ms frames at or above min_probability, in time order; empty when it never is

speech.description: With include ["speech"]: the speech probability of every 32 ms frame

from.description: Seconds where the first probability starts

probabilities.description: Speech probability 0–1, one per frame, in order

status.description: importing: not probed yet; processing: usable in edits, proxy still rendering; ready; failed

transcript.description: With include ["transcript"]: every word as {text, start, end, confidence}

aligned_by.description: The model that moved word edges to where the letters sound (English); null: the times are whisper's own, up to about a second off

words.description: Media seconds. Aligned words start and end within about 0.05 s of where their letters sound; an end on a soft consonant (s, t, k, f) or a breath can ring on up to about 0.1 s more. Short ums are often missing from the words; kind speech finds them as speech

confidence.description: 0–1: how sure whisper is of the word itself

timing_confidence.description: 0–1: how clearly the letters were heard between start and end; null: not aligned (digits, symbols, other languages), times fitted between neighbours

upload.description: media.import {source: {upload}}: where to send the file. It imports once the last byte arrives (the PUT answers with the job_id); media.get says where it stands

url.description: Signed: PUT the file here; no other credentials needed
media.get: a signed download of the file itself, once it has one

title: Get media
